verdict.reasoning: Independently verified against a fresh 300 dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v798/spec_p798.png) and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. PRINTED PAGE, read at 4x zoom on a tight crop of the figure: 'UNLOCK   file-name-1' followed by ONE tall square bracket spanning two stacked lines, RECORD over RECORDS. A pixel scan confirms the underline objectively - rows y=940-941 under x=295..455 are a solid rule (156/160 dark pixels across the full width of UNLOCK), while the same scan over file-name-1 (x=500..720) and over RECORD/RECORDS (x=760..960, y=860..1010) finds no rule of any kind. GLYPHS OF THE DELIMITER, as I see them: a plain left square bracket (top serif, full vertical stem, bottom serif) and its mirrored right partner, enclosing both words; there is no vertical bar inboard of either stem, so there are no choice indicators - the claim's reading of the bracket is correct and it correctly does NOT allege a lost choice indicator. MARKDOWN: the fenced block at lines 32335-32338 reproduces the words, their order and the optionality bracket faithfully, but carries no underline in any form - no <u>, no bold, no figure-notes paragraph. I read the entire page-798 slice; nothing anywhere on the page records which words are underlined. REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: (1) 'the text is present elsewhere' - it is not; the prose mentions UNLOCK but never records its typographic status. (2) 'this is mere formatting' - it is not decoration: 5.2.6 (lines 2631 and 2644) defines underlined uppercase = keyword/required word and non-underlined uppercase = optional word, so the underline is semantic metalanguage. (3) 'the file uniformly drops underlines inside code fences, so this is a global convention rather than a page-798 defect' - this was my strongest counter-argument and it fails on the evidence: the file carries 225 '> **Figure notes ...**' paragraphs, and the ones immediately bracketing this figure in the same chapter do exactly what is missing here - SUBTRACT Formats 1/2/3 at lines 32092/32109/32124 (just above), USE Formats 1/3/4 at 32561/32575/32585 and WRITE Formats 1/2 at 32977/33007 (just below), plus START 31762, STOP 31913, STRING 31973. Those notes explicitly enumerate which words are and are not underlined. So the remedy is genuinely established and densely applied in this very neighbourhood, and it is absent for UNLOCK. The claim quotes both sources accurately (its only error is a citation off-by-three: the fence is at 32335-32338, not 32332-32336, which is the anchor/heading pair) and the discrepancy is genuine.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with two corrections. (a) Line numbers: the fenced figure is at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32335-32338; 32332-32336 spans the <a id> anchor and the '### 14.9.47.2 General format' heading. (b) Severity is better recorded as minor/informational rather than structural. Nothing in the transcription is WRONG: the words, their order, the single tall plain bracket rendered as stacked [RECORD ] / [RECORDS], and the absence of choice-indicator bars all match the printed page exactly. What is missing is an annotation, not a correction - the figure-notes paragraph recording that UNLOCK is underlined (required word, 5.2.6.2 / lines 2631, 2644) and that file-name-1, RECORD and RECORDS are printed without underlines (optional words). The practical implementable loss is small, because a statement verb is required by definition and a non-underlined single word alone inside a bracket is syntactically indistinguishable from an underlined one inside the same bracket - RECORD, RECORDS or nothing, either way. The fidelity gap is nonetheless real and should be closed with the file's standard remedy: '> **Figure notes (UNLOCK statement general format).** `UNLOCK` is underlined in the printed standard (required word). `RECORD` and `RECORDS` are **not** underlined - they are optional words. The two alternatives are enclosed in a single plain bracket, so at most one may be specified; there are no choice indicators in this figure.' INCIDENTAL, outside the claim and not adjudicated here: the ASCII rendering as two per-line brackets differs from this file's usual tall-bracket drawing (the corner glyphs used in the adjacent UNSTRING figure) and could be misread as two independent sequential optional phrases; the figure-notes paragraph above would also neutralize that.
